implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy approved 2026-08-31 (P06). OT access procedures (SCADA accounts, vendor sessions) are due 2026-12-31.

Corporate and SaaS accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets. SCADA and HMI accounts are local to the SCADA servers and managed by the SCADA and Automation Supervisor. Gaps: removal takes up to 7 days for field staff and contractors; a shared vendor account and a shared HMI operator account exist; no access reviews.
evidence: IdP export; SCADA account list; termination tickets

implementation_statement: SaaS and cloud access is role-based. SCADA roles separate view-only, operator, and engineer rights. Field data capture app roles separate lease operators from accounting reviewers.
evidence: SaaS role matrix; SCADA role configuration

implementation_statement: The IT/OT firewall controls flows between the corporate and SCADA networks. Gap: rules allow broad access from corporate server subnets, including remote desktop to HMIs; no OT DMZ; one engineering workstation is dual-homed. OT DMZ due 2027-01-31.
Standard users have no local administrator rights on corporate endpoints. Gaps: the reservoir data share is open to all staff; Production Controllers can install software on HMIs.
Identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. HMIs lock the operator session after 5 failed attempts; the OCC is staffed 24x7, so lockout does not block operations.

Corporate endpoints lock after 10 minutes. OCC HMIs are exempt from screen lock by design (continuous alarm view) with badge-controlled room access as the compensating control; field office HMIs have no lock (gap).

Company users reach corporate systems through the VPN with MFA. Gap: the SCADA integrator uses an always-on third-party remote access tool on the SCADA primary server with a shared account and no MFA. Replacement jump host due 2026-11-30.
evidence: VPN policy; remote access tool inventory

implementation_statement: Office Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication; the SCADA network has no Wi-Fi. The 900 MHz field radio network has no message authentication (risk accepted, P01 R-004).
The 70 rugged tablets are enrolled in mobile device management with encryption, PIN, and remote wipe; the field data capture app requires sign-in through the identity provider.
Rules for integrator-owned laptops connecting to the SCADA network are being written with the transient device procedure (due 2026-12-31).
POL-05 sets training requirements. Training procedure for field staff is due 2026-12-31.
Office staff complete annual awareness training. Gap: field staff (about 190 people) receive none, and there are no phishing exercises.
Role-based OT security training for automation technicians and Production Controllers planned for 2027 Q1.

Sign-in, administrator, and cloud control-plane events are logged by the providers. SCADA servers log operator actions and alarms locally. Gap: firewall and SCADA security events are not defined or collected.
SCADA event records include time, workstation, and action. Gap: the shared HMI login means records do not identify the person.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Weekly review of identity provider and firewall events and monthly review of SCADA security events start with the central log collection (due 2027-03-31).
Identity provider keeps logs 30 days; firewall 7 days; SCADA logs overwrite at a fixed size. Target: 1 year centrally.
Providers generate audit records for SaaS and cloud; SCADA generates event records. OT network traffic is not recorded.
Independent control assessment performed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07); annual thereafter.
Information exchanges listed in SSP section 8. Gap: no interconnection terms with the gas gatherer (meter data) or the integrator.
Continuous monitoring strategy (quarterly metrics, OT monitoring, MDR) planned with the funded treatments; first quarterly report 2026-12-31.
Corporate endpoint baselines enforced in MDM. Gap: no documented baseline for SCADA servers, HMIs, or controller programs.
OT change control (change request, peer review, test, record) planned for 2026-12-31; corporate changes already use help desk tickets.
Controller programming rights will be limited to named engineer accounts and the program repository.
Corporate settings enforced by MDM. Gap: 3 field modems had default passwords and internet-facing management (found 2026-08-05); modem settings not standardized.
Unused services disabled on corporate servers. Gap: HMIs allow USB storage and have unneeded software installed by operators.
Corporate endpoints are inventoried in MDM and EDR. Gap: no OT inventory of RTUs, PLCs, drives, meters, modems, and radios.
Contingency planning procedure for SCADA due 2026-12-31 under POL-01.
The emergency response plan covers storms, spills, and H2S, including a manual-operations and shut-in procedure. Gap: no SCADA contingency plan for a cyber event.
First SCADA restore test on a spare server by 2026-10-30; quarterly thereafter; annual contingency tabletop.
Standby SCADA server moves to the South Florida field office (alternate processing site) by 2027-06-30.

Nightly SCADA server backups to a storage device in the OCC server room; daily cloud snapshots in the production account. Gaps: not isolated, not immutable, controller programs not backed up, never tested.
SCADA rebuild and restore procedure with the integrator, due 2026-12-31.

Unique accounts for all corporate and SaaS users. Gaps: shared HMI operator login and shared integrator account. The SP 800-82 Rev. 3 OT overlay (IA-2 discussion) accepts shared local accounts only with compensating physical security, personnel security, and auditing, and requires remote access to identify each individual before a shared account is used. Neither condition is documented or met today.
MFA for privileged cloud, SaaS, and VPN accounts; hardware keys for the 4 IT administrators. Gap: SCADA engineer and integrator access has no MFA.
MFA required for all non-privileged users of email, SaaS, and the VPN through conditional access.
Modem and RTU identification on the private cellular network by device identity will be enforced when modems are moved off the public network.
Identity provider enforces 14-character passwords and a banned-password list. Gaps: default modem passwords (3 sites); SCADA local passwords never changed since 2021; shared credentials.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-08-31.
P08 runbook approved 2026-08-31 for ransomware spreading toward SCADA. Not yet tested; no OT forensic support contracted.
Security incidents tracked in the help desk under a security category since 2026-09-01.
Reporting duties set in the P08 notification matrix (Florida notice, oil discharge reporting, voluntary CISA and FBI reports). Staff reporting line not yet known in the field.
Incident response plan (POL-03 and P08) approved; first tabletop by 2026-11-30.
Field maintenance scheduled in the ERP work order module. Gap: controller maintenance by the integrator is not recorded.
Nonlocal maintenance by the integrator happens through an always-on remote access tool without MFA, approval, or session records. Jump host with session recording due 2026-11-30.
USB storage will be blocked on HMIs and engineering workstations, with a scanning kiosk at the OCC for transfers (2026-12-31).
Badge access to the OCC and server room; well pads and tank batteries fenced and locked; RTU cabinets padlocked.
Cameras and badge logs at the OCC. Unmanned sites are checked on lease operator routes; no intrusion alarms (accepted, P01 R-023).
This SSP, approved 2026-08-31.
POL-05 Acceptable Use approved 2026-08-31; acknowledgments collected from office staff only so far.
Risk management strategy: SP 800-30 method, tolerance levels, and acceptance authority (P01; POL-01 4.4). A program-level control recorded here because the SSP inherits it from the company program.
Background checks before hire for OCC staff, automation technicians, IT staff, and drivers.
HR opens termination tickets; identity provider accounts disabled. Gap: up to 7 days for field staff; SCADA local accounts not included.
Security requirements for integrator and contractor personnel (named accounts, removal on reassignment) added at contract renewal.
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 and SP 800-82 Rev. 3 Appendix C (P01).
Quarterly authenticated scans of the corporate network. No active scanning in OT by design; passive OT vulnerability detection and advisory matching planned with the OT sensor.
Security schedule for OT and SaaS acquisitions (MFA, patch support, incident notice) to be added to contracts at renewal.
Production accounting vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 reviewed (P09). Other external services not assessed.
SCADA servers and HMIs run an operating system past end of vendor support; isolated behind the IT/OT firewall until the 2027-03-31 upgrade.
Firewalls at each office and between IT and OT; cloud network security rules. Gaps: broad IT/OT rules, no OT DMZ, dual-homed workstation, 3 internet-exposed modems.

TLS to SaaS; IPsec VPN to the cloud tenant. SCADA polling protocols are unencrypted inside the SCADA network and over the radio. The SP 800-82 Rev. 3 OT overlay (SC-8(1) discussion) allows compensating controls such as a protected conduit between components; the planned OT DMZ and segmentation provide this for the wired network, and radio integrity is an accepted risk (P01 R-004).

Provider encryption at rest in SaaS and cloud; laptops and tablets encrypted. Gaps: royalty owner exports in the shared file area; SCADA servers unencrypted (accepted for performance; physical access controlled).
Monthly corporate patching. OT patching ad hoc and limited by the unsupported operating system.
EDR on corporate laptops and desktops; signature antivirus on HMIs updated monthly by hand. Gap: EDR alerts unwatched after hours.
Passive OT network monitoring and 24x7 managed detection and response planned (2026-12-31 MDR; 2027-03-31 OT sensor).
Controller program comparison to the repository baseline and update-file hash checks planned with OT change control.
Controllers to be bought only from manufacturers or authorized distributors; secondary-market purchases stopped.
